entries.summary: Quoting Axios's report on a new OnMessage Inc. poll (commissioned by the Combat Antisemitism Movement's political arm) of 1,000 Republican voters in Iowa, New Hampshire, Nevada, and South Carolina, Price wrote, “You’re never going to believe this but it turns out that Vice President Vance and his foreign policy views are very popular with Republican Primary voters.” He attached a screenshot of Axios’s write-up, which this update also opened, stating that Vance was viewed 80% favorably and 19% unfavorably (net +61) among those voters, ahead of President Trump at 75/23 (net +52), and that 59% agreed with a statement Axios said “generally reflects the vice president's position”: “Israel has a right to exist, and America should remain its ally, however criticism of its government is legitimate, but when it turns into antisemitism that is unacceptable.” The poll was conducted Nov. 7–10, 2026 (margin of error ±3.1%). Axios noted that the survey was conducted for an advocacy group and that some of its questions are leading.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Account created August 2017 (526,350 followers, 3,280 following, 61,532 posts, blue verified). Engagement is modest relative to follower count (0.06%) and like-to-view ratio is about 1.4% (227 likes on 16,355 views), not an inflated pattern. The 27 replies opened were mostly unique text, with a mix of agreement and pushback and no copy-paste flood. A few very new, low-follower accounts appeared in the replies, but they were a small minority and did not drive the engagement.

entries.audience_sample: Replies opened were mixed and leaned toward skepticism of Price or the poll wording, with a minority backing Vance (e.g., “Vance is wise beyond his 42 years. We hit the jackpot with him”). Several challenged the claim or Vance (“When you strip out all detail from any statement it will poll as unobjectionable”; “The gop voters support Israel.  Vance does not”; “JD has been a big disappointment”; “He could NEVER win the general”). Prominent accounts (50,000+ followers or a major-org tie): Steve Cortes (@SteveCortes, 536,446), already in the tracker as a Vance supporter, quoted the post: “JD Vance’s America First foreign policy of realism and restraint is correct and very popular.” Douglass Mackey (@douglassmackey, 79,629) quoted it to say the surveyed statement was “crafted … as unobjectionable as possible.” Max Abrahms (@MaxAbrahms, 93,122), who describes himself in his bio as an international security professor, replied that Price “sound[ed] exactly like a leftwinger” for highlighting a question about whether “Israel has a right to exist.” None was added to the opposition list: Cortes is supportive, and Mackey and Abrahms were criticizing the poll wording or Price’s framing, not offering a critique of Vance’s record. Bradley Devlin (@bradleydevlin, 17,076) also quoted the post supportively (“Don’t let bad actors gaslight you, folks”) but is below the 50,000-follower threshold.

entries.source: The New York Times (Tyler Pager), syndicated by The Seattle Times
entries.summary: News report. Says Trump first called Vance's post-midterm analysis 'largely true' but has since complained to aides and allies that Vance should have said the decision to go to war with Iran was right, while praising Marco Rubio in private as a possible 2028 candidate (anonymous sources). Notes Trump pulled Vance from Iran peace talks to focus on a fraud investigation, that Vance says there is 'no daylight' with the president and will decide on 2028 'sometime next year,' and that allies say he is genuinely undecided. Quotes Alyssa Farah Griffin, Rob Flaherty and Chris Christie. Widely picked up on X (e.g., @DeItaone, @MarioNawfal, @RpsAgainstTrump, @LeadingReport).

authenticity.evidence: Newspaper report (NYT, syndicated text opened on The Seattle Times). Relies on anonymous sources; Vance's office declined to comment.

entries.audience_sample: Reaction under the most-shared X relays was split. Under @LeadingReport's post (1,010,690 followers; 989 likes, 53,524 views) most replies opened defended Vance ('Vance is 100% correct'; 'Trump reportedly frustrated with JD Vance for telling the truth'). Under @RyanAFournier's relay (separate entry) replies leaned against Vance. Ed Morrissey of Hot Air (@EdMorrissey, 65,144) questioned whether 'the New York Times' sources [are] spinning their own interests.'

entries.summary: Relaying the NYT report, wrote that 'Trump is having a meltdown behind closed doors' over Vance blaming the midterm loss on the Iran war, and that per the NYT 'Trump views Vance as a traitor for refusing to defend his decision to attack Iran' and has 'frozen Vance out.' The opened NYT text does not use the word 'traitor'; it says Trump complained Vance should have defended the decision and that Trump pulled Vance from Iran peace talks.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Blue-check account created April 2023 (bio: 'Constitutional Conservative. Journalist.'). 1,689 likes on 31,941 views is a high like-to-view ratio (about 5.3%), which can reflect a loyal follower base or coordinated liking; reply sample did not show duplicated text.

entries.audience_sample: Replies opened were mixed and mostly low-reach. Some attacked Vance ('Vance is a Palantir product'; 'willing to lie, back stab'), some doubted the NYT ('i don't trust anything the NYT says'), and some saw the distance helping Vance ('Ironically, that distance might help Vance'). Several replies contained antisemitic remarks. No 50K+ or major-organization accounts in the replies or quotes opened; the largest quoter was @Snowball1776 (44,612): 'Vance is the new Pence !!!'

entries.summary: Founder of Students for Trump (per bio) relayed the NYT report: Trump is 'reportedly growing frustrated' with Vance over blaming the Iran war for midterm losses, wanted Vance to defend the strike, and is 'reportedly sidelining Vance.' Relay without added commentary in the opened text.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only. Account created July 2010. Engagement 0.06% of followers, low rather than inflated; high reply share (27% of likes) indicates real argument in the thread.

entries.audience_sample: Replies opened leaned against Vance ('Vance is not ready'; 'Rubio is definitely more Presidential'; 'Vance is a weak fraud'), with a minority pushing back on the NYT or Fournier ('You quote NY Slime like it is a reputable source'; 'JD IS CORRECT'). No 50K+ or major-organization accounts in the replies opened.

entries.source: Brian Kilmeade (The Brian Kilmeade Show), reported by Mediaite
entries.theme: Iran war / 'forever war' / fitness for office
entries.summary: On his radio show Tuesday, Nov 17, Fox & Friends co-host Brian Kilmeade played Vance's Nov 16 Ingraham Angle answer that whatever Trump decides on Iran, 'there are going to be people who demand more, who want the war to go on indefinitely,' and that Trump 'is not going to let this become a forever war.' Kilmeade called that 'another straw man argument,' said 'there is not one person that I have ever met that wants an endless war,' and said of Vance: 'Never should have been vice president.' He also objected to Vance's post-midterm line that any honest conversation about the losses 'has to start with the Iran war.' Also reported by The Hill, TV Insider, HuffPost and The Daily Beast (opened). Kilmeade did not post the remarks on his own X account in this window; the follower count is his @kilmeade account.

authenticity.evidence: Radio/podcast remarks reported by several outlets (Mediaite, The Hill, TV Insider, HuffPost, Daily Beast pages opened). The most-shared X clip, by Daily Caller's John Loftus (@JohnCFLoftus1, 2,858 followers, account created March 2020), had 267 likes, 65 reposts, 42 replies, 14 quotes and 66,182 views as of this update: far beyond the poster's follower base, which is consistent with organic pickup by larger accounts quoting it rather than a bot push; heuristic only.

entries.audience_sample: Reaction under the Loftus clip and its quotes leaned toward pushing back on Kilmeade, i.e., defending Vance (e.g., 'Kilmeade is an idiot. Trump's war on Iran for Israel lost us the mid terms'), with a minority agreeing ('Kilmeade is correct'). Prominent quoters: former Rep. Barbara Comstock (39,422 followers; former VA-10 congresswoman) — 'So @JDVance bogus straw men arguments annoy everyone?' (74 likes, 7,865 views); Guardian media reporter Jeremy Barr (29,080) — 'one of the strongest critiques I've seen in a while' (reporter's observation, not an endorsement; 33 likes, 5,704 views); The Federalist senior editor John Daniel Davidson (39,716) pushed back on Kilmeade: 'What's aggravating is the idiotic neocon riposte that "no one's calling for a forever war"'; Douglass Mackey (79,635) also pushed back: 'wars can drag on for years once you start them'; @a_newsman (14,542) — 'Murdoch sending out Brian Kilmeade... to sell wars' (140 likes). Steve Cortes's supportive counter-post (separate entry) quoted the clip.

entries.summary: Former Republican Rep. Barbara Comstock (VA-10, per her bio) said Americans are alarmed by the wave of outages 'because we have no adults in this Admin,' calling Vance 'an inexperienced child from a dysfunctional family with no expertise' who 'spends most of his time on podcasts, Fox, and vacations,' and suggested 'serious Senate Republicans may think about staging an intervention.' On Nov 18 she also quoted the Kilmeade clip ('So @JDVance bogus straw men arguments annoy everyone?') and reposted an On Point poll showing Ossoff leading Vance 50–37.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Account created May 2009 with 39,422 followers, 4,527 following and 41,173 posts; bio identifies her as a former VA-10 Representative. Engagement (3.4% of followers, 7.7% of views) is high but consistent with a viral anti-administration post; quotes opened were short endorsements ('This, This, This!!!', 'Amen') from established small accounts plus one repeated multi-post outage thread; no copy-paste flood.

entries.audience_sample: Replies opened mostly agreed with her (e.g., 'The administration is clueless'), with some pushback from Trump supporters ('It's happening worldwide'). No 50K+ or major-organization accounts were found among the replies and quotes opened; the largest quote was by a former VOA host (@by_xubo, 26,118 followers) translating the post into Chinese.

No 50K+ or major-organization accounts were found in the replies opened.

The post targets Vance's backers rather than Vance himself, so it is logged as mixed and is not counted as a new critical item for Levin.

Several replies contained antisemitic remarks from small accounts. The largest replier was the automated @grok account answering side questions; no 50K+ human or major-organization accounts were found.

entries.summary: In a thread asking which elected Republican besides Trump has the most “raw political talent” (charisma and “vibes,” not policy agreement), Walsh surveyed replies and posted a 24-hour poll of the four names that came up most: Vance, Rubio, Gill, and DeSantis. A later reply in the comments identified Gill as Rep. Brandon Gill. Final result (poll closed Nov 18, 2026, 11:13 AM PT; 67,220 votes): Rubio 31,794 (47.3%), DeSantis 19,338 (28.8%), Gill 8,635 (12.8%), Vance 7,453 (11.1%). Vance finished last. Walsh does not endorse or attack Vance in the thread; he includes him as one of the names mentioned. The original question post (8:21 AM PT, Nov 17) had 6,486 likes, 208 reposts, 228 quotes, 5,627 replies, 566 bookmarks and 3,021,996 views at close.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof; X poll votes are anonymous, so votes are judged only indirectly. (1) Vote shares were stable to the end: from the earlier snapshot (59,262 votes) to the close (67,220), the late 7,958 votes split Rubio 49.9%, DeSantis 26.8%, Gill 12.2%, Vance 11.2%, versus 46.9 / 29.0 / 12.9 / 11.1% before; no late surge for any name. The final order also matches a public count of names in the replies (Rubio 1,293, DeSantis 861, Gill 656, Vance 347, from @frontrunnershow, a 2-week-old 435-follower account, so treat as rough). (2) Sampled commenters look like real accounts: 106 unique authors across 101 replies and 23 quote-posts; median account age about 4.7 years for repliers; 3 of 83 repliers had under 10 followers, 2 had default avatars, 2 had digit-string handles, 10 were created in 2026; no copy-paste flood (the most repeated reply was just “Marco Rubio,” 4 times). (3) Traffic toward Rubio was driven by big quote-posts rather than anonymous accounts: Laura Loomer’s quote (“Marco Rubio… not even a contest”) reached 143,535 views, 8,930 likes and 814 reposts, and Pino Americano’s poll quote reached 23,610 views and 121 reposts. Caveat: among 62 sampled reposters of the Pino quote, 16 (26%) average more than 100 posts a day and 7 use default avatars, a pattern typical of high-volume retweet accounts; that is amplification, not evidence of vote stuffing.

entries.audience_sample: Quotes and replies opened leaned toward Rubio or DeSantis rather than Vance; in the sample, Rubio was named in 21 replies, DeSantis 14, Gill 9, Vance 4. Prominent commenters (50K+ followers or major-org tie), as fetched at close: Laura Loomer (@LauraLoomer, 1,935,729 followers; LOOMERED founder) replied “Marco Rubio” (2,403 likes, 39,175 views) and quoted the question: “Marco Rubio. And it’s not even a contest.” (8,930 likes, 814 reposts, 560 replies, 143,535 views) — pro-Rubio over Vance. Tomi Lahren (@TomiLahren, 2,865,491; OutKick/Fox News host) replied she wants someone who “stays true to the values and gets shit done,” naming DeSantis (2,245 likes, 180,478 views) — a preference, not a Vance critique; Walsh replied, “Yeah but that wasn’t my question.” Three Year Letterman (@3YearLetterman, 486,915; satire account) joked “Gerald Ford” (99 likes) — no stance. Kosher (@koshercockney, 183,833) quoted: “Wow. Nobody likes Vance.” (248 likes, 4,007 views) — critical. Pino Americano (@PinoAmericano, 117,273) quoted the poll: “JD Vance is nearly off the stage. Let’s go Rubio!” (1,187 likes, 121 reposts, 23,610 views) — critical. Walsh also posted a follow-up asking for non-politicians who could run in 2028 (1,737 likes, 682,381 views). Reply-to-like ratio on the poll post is 117%.

entries.summary: Former JD Vance supporter says Vance’s “forever wars” talking points on Iran are getting tiring; argues Vance is talking in campaign phrases rather than as a serious thinker, and contrasts him with Marco Rubio.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Seed post from a long-standing verified account (created 2008, 183K followers). Engagement rate 1.06% of followers and 5.6% of views is in line for a mid-size political account, not an out-of-range spike. A sample of 11 original quote-posts showed a mix of agreement and pushback (roughly half supportive of the criticism), from mostly older accounts with custom avatars and modest followings. One newer digit-suffix account appeared in the sample. No copy-paste flood observed in the quotes opened.

entries.audience_sample: Of 11 original quotes opened, about half agreed with the criticism; several pushed back that the public does not want a prolonged Middle East war. Reply-to-like ratio 18%.

entries.summary: Writes that Vance, whom he once held in high esteem, surveyed the midterm “electoral massacre” and found “a scapegoat many others have found for millennia: the Jews,” calling it “rank cowardice.” Links his FrontPage Magazine column.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Verified pundit account (created 2009, 170K followers). 255K views and a 2.1% engagement rate vs. followers are high but plausible for a controversy post, not an inexplicable spike. A 25-reposter sample included many issue-aligned (pro-Israel) accounts, a mix of older and newer profiles, about 5 default avatars, several name-plus-digits handles, and at least one very new 2026 account with few followers and high posting volume. No identical copy-paste replies were documented in the sample opened. High reply-to-like ratio (28%) and a large opposing quote (Auron MacIntyre, 3,615 likes) indicate substantial pushback, not one-sided amplification.

entries.audience_sample: Low reply ratio (55 replies on 3,615 likes) suggests more agreement than argument in the sample of metrics, unlike the Hammer post it quotes.

Small official-style reporter account (5.6K followers) but very high views (188K) and a 19.3% engagement rate vs. followers, which is high relative to the account size—plausible for a viral congressman quote, but the ratio is elevated. High reply-to-like ratio (42%) indicates heavy argument, not quiet amplification. Included because it reports a notable elected official, even though the reporter is under the 50K-follower guideline.

Two smaller accounts posted nearly identical wording later; that copy-paste cluster is noted but those accounts were not added as entries (under the size cutoff).

entries.summary: Originating post. Vance says 2024 Trump/Vance voters showed up but many voted Democratic in 2026. Citing an unnamed pollster, he lists four reasons those voters gave for coming back: end the war; focus on cost of living/inflation; put America First; “Change our relationship to Israel.” He adds, “The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night.”

Extraordinary absolute reach (73.5M views, 285K likes) with a high 7.3% engagement rate vs. 5.6M followers, consistent with a major post-election statement from a sitting VP, not a mid-tier account suddenly going viral. 69K replies and 21K quotes indicate a very large mixed conversation; those replies were not fully coded.

entries.audience_sample: Not coded in full (69,387 replies, 21,254 quotes). High absolute discussion volume. Donald Trump Jr. publicly endorsed the post.

entries.summary: Josh Hammer column, “JD Vance Scapegoats the Jews.” Argues Vance’s post-election claim that the Iran war and a changed U.S.-Israel relationship helped cause Republican losses amounted to blaming Jews or Israel.
